subject: general
question: The lengths of the parallel sides of a trapezium are 10 cm and 20 cm. If the distance between these parallel lines is 5 cm, then what is the area of the trapezium?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a **trapezium** is the product of the **average of parallel sides** and the **distance** between them.

Average of parallel sides = (10 + 20) ÷ 2 = 15 cm

Area = 15 × 5 = 75 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 75 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first parallel side (a) = **10 cm**

Length of second parallel side (b) = **20 cm**

Height or distance between sides (h) = **5 cm**

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7003695699fc19ad599c21e275a1ab95c5772c5a568547e0d7b036c0a48ffe3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (10 + 20) × 5

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 30 × 5

⇒ Area = 15 × 5

⇒ Area = 75 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 75 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Trapezium

The total boundary of the trapezium is the sum of all its four sides: **Perimeter = a + b + c + d**.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium where the **non-parallel sides** are equal in length. In this case, the base angles are also equal.

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Its length is **(a + b) ÷ 2**.</p
